label: PF Backlog 671
title: EDP: fail closed for unlisted backlog scopes when DB mode is on
body: Prevent silent file fallback for unlisted scopes; require explicit off/legacy mode.

decisions.note: HIL directed continuing in the stated order; delta review approved.
HIL approved Gate 1; implement fail-closed unlisted-scope guard.

brief.problem: Unlisted scopes silently stay file-authoritative when PF_BACKLOG_DB=on.
brief.what_adds: DB mode fail-closed for unlisted scopes; explicit off for legacy file mode.
brief.why: Prevents split authority and silent persistence outside DB.

BLOCKER: FR-3 (AC-3) is self-contradictory: preconditions say "DB mode on", acceptance says "Given DB on ... Then it fails closed", and the FR-3 title/triggers repeat on-mode guard behavior — the approved AC-3 (off mode keeps file authority) is not actually specified or testable as written.

No distinct evidence/tests exist for AC-4's operator-recovery runbook path; all four ACs point to one pytest command that cannot demonstrate runbook coverage (stop condition "Missing tests for read/write/delete/ID" is unproven).
MAJOR: `PF_BACKLOG_DB` valid values include `dual` and `shadow`, but the operation_matrix/failure_matrix only define `on` and `off` behavior for unlisted scopes — unlisted-scope semantics under dual/shadow are unspecified, risking a silent file fallback through an undefined mode.
Design does not address CL-011: no runtime role posture (NOSUPERUSER/NOBYPASSRLS) or tenant-binding proof for the guard, despite `security_threat_model` and `rls_tenant` being marked APPLICABLE.

Design guardrail checklist items 2 (availability/SPOF: worker/DB down behavior, on-startup check), 4 (blast radius/dry-run), 5 (id/sequence invariants for ID-allocation path) are unanswered in the design pack.
MINOR: Rollback is inconsistent: item says "Revert the change", design says "Set PF_BACKLOG_DB=off explicitly" — two different rollback procedures with no precedence stated.
Config contract `startup_validation` for `PF_BACKLOG_DB` is "operation" (lazy) rather than on-startup, weakening CL-014-style defence-in-depth; failure surfaces only at first use.
Observability is limited to "error code logged with scope" — no metric/counter for `BACKLOG_DB_SCOPE_UNLISTED` occurrences, so fail-closed spikes are not alertable.
`affected_files`/`in_scope` contain "Not specified." placeholders; CL-016 separation of prerequisites (BI-PF-1531) from changed files is not explicit in scope.
Off-mode operation_matrix covers only read/write for unlisted scopes; delete/ID off-mode behavior is unlisted despite AC-2/AC-4 covering those paths.
NIT: Error taxonomy defines only `BACKLOG_DB_SCOPE_UNLISTED`; consider whether mode/allowlist misconfiguration (`BACKLOG_DB_MODE_INVALID`) needs an equivalent documented recovery step in the runbook.
`ac_evidence.sha` values are "candidate" rather than pinned SHAs; traceability is weaker than a content-addressed evidence reference.
SUMMARY: Direction is right (fail closed, no silent fallback, explicit off), but AC-3 is specified inconsistently within FR-3 itself and AC-4's runbook/test evidence is not concretely demonstrated — these must be fixed before Gate 1.5.
Undefined dual/shadow semantics for unlisted scopes is the top residual risk of reintroducing the silent file fallback this item exists to remove.

Guardrail gaps (RLS/role posture, startup validation, availability/invariants) and a dual rollback definition need design answers; no schema/API/language-rule violations found in the declared file set.

BLOCKER: Disposition ACTIONED for the AC-4 evidence finding is not reflected in data: `test_matrix` still lists the identical pytest command for AC-1..AC-4 and `ac_evidence` for all four ACs share one sha (`69dd9c33`) and one artifact (`operator-recovery.md`) — guardrail 13 (distinct executable test or runbook artifact per AC) is still unmet, so AC-4 runbook coverage remains unproven.
MAJOR: FR-4's `acceptance` is still "Given DB on When unlisted AC-4 path runs Then it fails closed", which does not match AC-4 (tests and runbook cover read/write/delete/ID paths and operator recovery) — guardrail 11 AC/FR one-to-one correspondence remains unsatisfied (only FR-3 was corrected).
MINOR: Disposition for the observability finding is ACTIONED but `design_pack.observability` still contains only "Structured ... error with scope key; precheck/test evidence" — no metric/counter or alertability for `BACKLOG_DB_SCOPE_UNLISTED` occurrences was added.
`affected_components` still reads `["Not specified."]`; CL-016's separation of prerequisites (BI-PF-1531) from changed components remains only partially actioned (`affected_files` is now populated).
NIT: FR-1/FR-2/FR-4 `title` values are truncated mid-string ("...raise BACKLOG_DB_SCOPE_U"), weakening traceability readability in the spec pack.
SUMMARY: Guardrails on mode completeness (dual/shadow), FR-3/off-mode, security posture, rollback, startup validation, and guardrail checklist items are genuinely addressed in this revision.

The two blockers/majors that remain are evidence and AC/FR traceability: a single shared evidence artifact + single test command still backs all four ACs, and FR-4's outcome text still does not describe AC-4's test/runbook requirement.
Gate should not pass until AC-4 has a distinct, executable runbook/recovery artifact reference and FR-4's acceptance is rewritten to match AC-4.

BLOCKER: `ac_evidence` for AC-1..AC-4 all carry the identical sha `3e273784` while pointing at four different artifacts (`AC-1.md`..`AC-4.md`) — distinct files cannot share one content hash; guardrail 13 (evidence quality/distinct evidence) is not genuinely satisfied, and the prior ACTIONED disposition's fix is not provable from the data.
MAJOR: `affected_components` in the delta drops `config`, yet the design's own `config_contract` (`PF_BACKLOG_DB_SCOPES`, `config/env-flags.json`) and `affected_files` still include a config change — changed-scope declaration now contradicts the unchanged contract rows in the same design (CL-016 consistency).

`design_pack.coverage` for AC-3 lists `failure_cases: ["BACKLOG_DB_SCOPE_UNLISTED"]` although AC-3/FR-3 expects file authority with `errors: "none"` — AC/FR contract mismatch persists in the coverage rows (guardrail 11).
MINOR: `test_matrix` AC-4 `kind` is "runbook" but the row's `test` is a pytest `-k ac4` invocation, not a runbook execution/evidence step; distinctness between AC-4 runbook proof and the AC-1..AC-3 unit tests rests solely on `-k` filtering.
`design_pack.coverage` for AC-4 likewise lists a unit-style pytest command as the sole evidence for a "tests and runbook + operator recovery" contract.
NIT: All four coverage rows reuse identical `adapter`, `entrypoint`, and `tests` values, so the rows read as copy-paste and offer no per-AC signal in review.
SUMMARY: Prior findings are correctly dispositioned (distinct evidence files, FR-4 acceptance, observability counter/alert, populated components, untruncated titles), but the delta reintroduces evidence-integrity risk: one shared sha across four artifacts. Also fix the AC-3 failure_cases mismatch and restore `config` to affected components before Gate 1.5.

MINOR: `functional_spec.traceability` (changed field) still records AC-4 evidence as only `test-framework/tests/pipeline/test_backlog_db_cutover.py`, while `design_pack.test_matrix`/`coverage` in the same delta point AC-4 at `engineering/evidence/BI-PF-1534/operator-recovery.md`; the traceability rows were not synced with the changed test rows.

`design_pack.coverage` AC-1 sets `runtime_capability: true` while AC-2 (the primary write/delete/ID fail-closed guard) sets `false`; the flag's semantics are inconsistent across rows for what is the same guard implementation.
NIT: `functional_spec.traceability` and FR `verification` commands use bare `pytest -q` without the `-k acN` selectors used in `test_matrix`, so the traceability commands do not pinpoint the per-AC test they claim to trace.
`config_contract` for `PF_BACKLOG_DB_SCOPES` uses `invalid_behavior: "unlisted fail closed"` rather than an explicit error code, unlike `PF_BACKLOG_DB`'s `BACKLOG_DB_MODE_INVALID`.
SUMMARY: Delta resolves all six prior findings: evidence SHAs are now distinct, `config` restored to `affected_components`, AC-3 `failure_cases` corrected to `none`, and AC-4 runbook artifact wired into test_matrix/coverage.
Residual issues are traceability-row sync and flag semantics; no AC/security/data-loss blockers.

BLOCKER: Evidence commands `pytest -k ac1/ac2/ac3/ac4` match no test names in the diff (`test_unlisted_scope_fails_closed`, `test_id_allocator_scope_gate`, etc.), so AC-1–AC-3 evidence is invalid (pytest deselects all → exit 5, not PASS); distinct AC-keyed tests are missing.

AC-4 runbook `engineering/evidence/BI-PF-1534/operator-recovery.md` is absent from the diff and evidence set; declared file `docs/BACKLOG-DB-SSOT.md` is unchanged, so operator recovery is not covered (Gate stop condition: "Missing tests for read/write/delete/ID" also unmet — no delete-path test).

Declared files `config/env-flags.json` and `docs/BACKLOG-DB-SSOT.md` are not updated: `PF_BACKLOG_DB` purpose still says only "on=DB for PF_BACKLOG_DB_SCOPES" with no unlisted fail-closed contract, so operators get no discoverable recovery path.
MAJOR: Design observability contract unmet: no `backlog_db_scope_unlisted_total` counter or structured log; a bare `RuntimeError` string is thrown, giving no machine-readable metric/alert lead-time for sustained unlisted-scope failures.
AC-3 only asserts `_db_for(...) is False` in off mode; no test proves off-mode unlisted read/write/delete actually performs file authority (write path untested for the off/unlisted case).

`core/id_allocator.py` is a declared affected file but is unchanged; the test only exercises it transitively — if `_db_enabled` does not delegate to the guarded resolver, ID fail-closed is unproven at the ID layer itself.
MINOR: `_DB_WARNED_SCOPES` (and its import/use) is now dead code left behind by the change.
`RuntimeError` is a generic type; a dedicated exception carrying a stable `BACKLOG_DB_SCOPE_UNLISTED` code/attributes would let callers and tests discriminate without string matching.
`test_id_allocator_scope_gate` uses try/except/else instead of `pytest.raises`, inconsistent with the sibling test and less precise on failure diagnostics.
NIT: `spec_quality_check.py` uses compressed single-line style (`CFG=...`, `def cfg(): return ...`) inconsistent with the referenced Python style guide.

[OUT_OF_SCOPE] Diff contains unrelated gate wiring (`gate1_check.py`, `precheck.py`, new `spec_quality_check.py`, `test_spec_chain.py`) outside the declared review files; flagged for scope-guard hygiene, not judged here.
SUMMARY: Fail-closed guard in `_db_for`/`db_authority_enabled` is directionally correct and matches the on/dual/shadow vs off matrix, but the delivery does not meet AC-1–AC-4 as evidenced: no AC-keyed tests, no operator-recovery runbook, no delete-path test, and declared config/docs files untouched.
Top risks: unverifiable acceptance evidence (invalid `-k ac1..ac4` commands), missing operator runbook for the new hard-failure mode, and absent observability counter required by the approved design.
Recommend: add distinct AC-keyed tests (read/write/delete/ID + off-mode file proof), ship the runbook and env-flag/doc updates, and emit the structured error/counter before approval.

BLOCKER: AC-4 test resolves the runbook via CWD-relative `Path("engineering/evidence/BI-PF-1534/operator-recovery.md")`, but its evidence command (`python -m pytest test-framework/...`) must run from `product-forge/`, while `engineering/` is repo-root (same convention as `config/`, `docs/`). Under the documented command the path does not resolve → FileNotFoundError, so AC-4 evidence fails.
MAJOR: Design observability contract still unmet: `_DB_UNLISTED_COUNT`/`scope_unlisted_count()` have zero callers and zero test assertions — no `backlog_db_scope_unlisted_total` metric export or alert, so sustained-failure lead-time is absent (this merely replaces the removed dead `_DB_WARNED_SCOPES` with new dead state).

AC-2 ID coverage only asserts `id_allocator._db_enabled` raises; no test drives an actual id-reserve/allocation entrypoint, so the design invariant "unlisted ID allocation raises before Git/local fallback" remains unproven at the allocation path.
AC-4 test only greps for `PF_BACKLOG_DB=off` and `PF_BACKLOG_DB_SCOPES` substrings; it does not verify the runbook covers read/write/delete/ID recovery as the AC requires, so a stub runbook passes.
MINOR: AC-3 exercises only the write path; off-mode unlisted read/delete/ID (explicitly in the design `operation_matrix`) are untested.
Only `PF_BACKLOG_DB=on` is tested; `dual`/`shadow` + unlisted (operation_matrix expects raise) have no coverage.
AC-2 `backlog._save_item("ignored", {"scope":"unlisted_ac2"})` passes conflicting scope keys; the test can pass on the positional key without proving the item-scope guard.
Tests assert only the exception type/message; none proves "no file/DB access before the guard" (design invariant "On + unlisted never touches files").
`import logging` is executed inside `_raise_unlisted` on every failure path instead of module level.
NIT: Test lines use semicolon-compressed `monkeypatch.setenv(...); monkeypatch.setenv(...)` style, inconsistent with the referenced Python style guide.
Log line repeats `code=BACKLOG_DB_SCOPE_UNLISTED` already present in the message prefix; error message and log format could share one structured source.
`_DB_UNLISTED_COUNT` is an unsynchronized, non-resettable process global (test/parallel-worker leakage if ever exposed as a metric).
SUMMARY: Delta correctly consolidates the unlisted-scope raise into `_raise_unlisted` with logging and adds AC-keyed tests, resolving prior dead-code and evidence-naming findings.

Top risks: the AC-4 runbook test is CWD-incompatible with its own evidence command (likely failing AC-4), the new counter is dead state that does not satisfy the design's metric/alert contract, and AC-2/AC-3 mode+path coverage (ID allocation fallback, off-mode read/delete/ID, dual/shadow) remains partial.
Recommend fixing the runbook path resolution, exporting/testing the counter, and adding allocation-path and off-mode read/delete tests before gate pass.
